purpose: Resolve whether FORWARD oracle messages saying 'Field removed' indicate leaked removal mutations or the oracle's reversed FORWARD comparison of genuine base-to-candidate additions.

method.schema_evidence: For every saved oracle-run directory, compare generated-contract/v1.json to generated-contract/v2.json recursively. Classify addition_only only when candidate properties contain added keys, base contains no removed keys, and deleting only those added properties makes candidate exactly equal to base after canonical object-key sorting.
method.optional_check: Verify each added key is absent from candidate.required.
method.profile_check: Verify open inputs do not set root additionalProperties=false and closed inputs do.
method.unique_pair_identity: SHA-256 of canonical base JSON plus canonical candidate JSON.
method.report_evidence: Read the already-persisted optional-open.json and optional-closed.json reports; do not rerun the JAR.

direction_explanation.generator: src/generation/mutation.rs clones base and inserts dcg_generated_optional_{string,integer,boolean,array} into candidate.properties without adding the key to required.
direction_explanation.oracle: DefaultCompatibilityEngine evaluates FORWARD by calling diff(candidate, base), then prefixes the resulting backward-rule messages with [FORWARD]. Therefore a property added from v1/base to v2/candidate is intentionally seen as removed in the candidate-to-base FORWARD diff.

representativeness.reason: Its baseline/FORWARD rows cover the same four genuine base-to-candidate optional additions as every sampled family: string, integer, boolean, and array. The 'Field removed' text is the expected FORWARD diff rendering, not an actual generated removal.

resolution.clarification: The cited trace was a genuine addition but was described without explaining the oracle's reversed FORWARD diff direction. Its wording was misleading in the report narrative, not evidence of a removal mutation.
